baiera.claim: Baiera genus-level fossil leaf specimen interpretation grounded in one museum CH106 outline, labelled Baiera asadai by the museum. Not a taxonomic redetermination, exact replica, whole plant or precise age/locality assertion. Museum Upper Jurassic/Jehol association is contradictory with modern Early Cretaceous Jehol literature and is explicitly not adopted. No Sphenobaiera or Baiera multipartita morphology substituted.
baiera.observation: Personally read museum label Baiera asadai Yabe et Oishi, Ginkgophyta, CH106 specimen photograph. Actual pixels show a narrow basal petiole opening into deeply separated flat long wedge/ribbon lobes, divided unevenly toward tips, preserved on gray slab. Chosen specimen only; no whole-tree features. Museum lists Upper Jurassic/Jehol/Liaoning and 11.5cm; PNAS2021 DOI10.1073/pnas.2107859118 abstract explicitly identifies Jehol as Early Cretaceous, so specimen age/locality is unresolved, not relabelled automatically. Wiley DOI10.1111/nph.20154 read only as comparison: Late Triassic B.multipartita is different material and not used for selected outline.
features: one flattened deeply divided fan leaf with basal petiole
unequal flat branching wedge lobes and open gaps
low fossil relief on thin original irregular slab
no cylindrical needles, generic intact Ginkgo fan, tree or reproductive organs
baiera.decisions: CH106-like original silhouette uses one central basal wedge and unequal forked flat lobes. Fossil carbonized brown relief has finite thickness, not living green foliage. Original supporting shale slab, irregular nonrepeating edge. Petiole and lobe breadths accentuated gently for readability; no invented diagnostic venation or leaf-mining damage. Geometry meters are nominal teaching-prop scale, not a claim of scanned dimensions. Concept inspected: concept basal lobe blades are broader and more decorative than CH106; correct geometry to narrower flat strips and deeper uneven divisions, avoid transferring concept broad fan into fossil claim. Preserve seven-ish terminal tips, not exact division count.

transverse-dune-ridge.claim: Original generic transverse sand-dune ridge geological process analogue. One laterally continuous asymmetric ridge, not a named locality, era, measured aeolian simulation or a rotated linear dune.
transverse-dune-ridge.observation: Personally read Lancaster2009 NPS-hosted article, dune morphology paragraphs and caption. Actual Figure4 pixels show transverse/crescentic ridge perpendicular to wind with asymmetric cross section; Figure5A/B show laterally linked crescentic forms, B broadly continuous ridges. Figure5D/E are linear forms; prose panel lettering conflicts with caption, so actual labels govern. CopyrightGSA consult-only. Batch70 linear-dune inspected only as duplicate guard, no source mesh or geometry reused.
features: single wide laterally continuous slightly sinuous sharp crest
uninterrupted substantially shorter steep leeward slipface
asymmetric cross section visible in clay, not duplicated barchans or narrow linear ridge
transverse-dune-ridge.decisions: Across X one continuous crest with small natural height and plan sinuosity. Wind travels +Y; stoss from Y=-52 to crest nearY=9, slipface toY=34: ramp run61 versus slipface25 for nominal height14.5, about13deg versus30deg. Sand cutaway extends windward and leeward. No painted bands, repetitive surface tiles, vegetation or barchan horns. Different structure from batch70 long narrow near-symmetric linear dune; no copied geometry. Concept inspected: asymmetry and continuous slipface are usable; reduce concept steep near-vertical look to approximately angle-of-repose30degrees with no regular sawtooth crest.

braided-river-reach.claim: Original generic shallow braided alluvial river reach, a static process analogue. Not a Snake River replica, named-site survey, precise age, hydrologic simulation or ecosystem reconstruction.
braided-river-reach.observation: Personally read NPS GrandTeton relative-elevation article: abundant coarse sediment, varying discharge, exposed midchannel bars and interweaving multithread channels. Personally inspected actual NPS/Potter fall photograph, not just LiDAR visualization: broad exposed tapered gravel bars divide blue shallow flow into unequal joining arms; bars and banks are irregular and asymmetric.
features: connected shallow inset multithread water network
multiple genuine splitting and rejoining nodes
several unequal tapered natural exposed sediment bars
continuous physical floodplain with channel banks below dry bar tops, no decorative islands on one meander
braided-river-reach.decisions: Long-axis Y flow; branch network repeatedly splits and rejoins around three offset bar groups and a cross-connecting arm. Water surface kept below continuous bank terrain and unequal exposed bar crests; terrain is carved by distance to the same branch-network centerlines. Bar forms arise in network voids rather than separate discs placed on a water sheet. Closed terrain cutaway with natural low relief and a few embedded faceted gravel stones. No vegetation required for bare sediment reference scope. Concept inspected: connectivity useful, but concept has overly repeated symmetric almond bars. Correct final branch network to unequal asymmetric widths, staggered junctions and differently shaped bars, not copy those ovals.

geode-cavity.claim: Original generic free rounded geode nodule with enclosing rind and hollow inward-quartz-lined cavity; deliberate front/top display wedge opening removes about one third of shell to expose interior. Not an intact sealed geode, bedrock crystal pocket, dogtooth spar cavity, exact specimen, locality or age reconstruction.
geode-cavity.observation: Personally read UtahGeologicalSurvey Dugway page: roughly spherical geodes, crystal-lined cavities, most hollow and quartz common; actual geodes3 photograph shows three opened nodules with enclosing rind and pale lining. Personally read IowaGeologicalSurvey page and inspected open Keokuk geode actual photograph: lumpy rounded enclosing exterior, pale small quartz crystals lining irregular inward hollow. Utah text has erroneous Bonneville phrase thousand years; no precise ages propagated. Original FortMatanzas coquina reference is irrelevant and provides NO support for geodes; original inventory remains unchanged.
features: free rounded finite enclosing nodule, not continuous bedrock
deliberate limited front/top display opening with honest broken/cut rim
small unequal inward-pointing quartz crystals attached to inner wall, not outward spikes or filled solid
geode-cavity.decisions: Retain roughly two-thirds of rounded lumpy shell including complete back and underside, remove bounded front/top wedge for visibility. Wall has exterior rind, finite thickness and pale inner chalcedony liner. Crystals attach to inner concave surface and point toward cavity center, irregular spacing/size, short enough to preserve empty hollow; mostly creamy quartz, no unsupported amethyst claim. Cut opening is a deliberate educational display convention frozen before modeling; not claimed natural break or bedrock cave. No pedestal or slab. Concept inspected: rounded free enclosing nodule and hollow read correctly. Concept crystals too large/coarse; final lining uses substantially smaller unequal quartz crystals, preserving empty inward hollow. Opening reinterpreted as honest removed front/top display cap, no natural break claim.
